notes: Line-by-line check. NHS excerpts support: first thing in the morning on an empty stomach with plain tap water (not mineral water, tea, coffee, juice or milk), stay upright 30 minutes, common GI effects and muscle/joint/bone pain, gullet irritation with stop-and-see-doctor advice for worsening heartburn/chest pain, jaw problems (tell dentist), thigh/groin/hip pain to report. No new dose or frequency figure was added (70 mg weekly is not stated; 30-minute upright period is the NHS figure and was implied by the pre-patch 'inability to sit upright' caution). The administration technique is retained because it is NHS-stated, safety-critical and the pre-patch record already referred to 'the dosing instructions'. 'Flu-like illness after the first zoledronic acid infusion' predates the patch. Paget disease use is standard (MedlinePlus). No protected field (review, depth, conditionCautions, targets) changed; references https on nhs.uk/medlineplus.
